title: Saint-honor differs only in degree from civil honor, but in kind from divine worship
source_text: XI. Sed quantalibet sit illa observantia qua colere & honorare debemus quos Deus in hac vita salutifera gratia ornavit, & in altera gloria coronavit, pertendunt illam solo gradu differre ab honore illo quo colere tenemur eos qui potestate & dignitate civili, aut naturali aliqua virtute atque praestantia, inter alios eminent & excellunt; ab eo vero quem divina Majestas postulat & exigit toto genere discrepare.
pass_a_gloss: But however great that observance may be by which we ought to cultivate and honor those whom God has adorned in this life with saving grace and crowned with glory in the other, they maintain that it differs only in degree from that honor by which we are bound to cultivate those who stand out and excel among others by civil power and dignity, or by some natural virtue and excellence; but that it differs in its whole kind from that which the divine majesty demands and requires.
pass_b_english: However high the respect due to people adorned with saving grace and crowned with glory, the Reformed hold it differs from ordinary civil honor only by degree.
The people compared are those who excel by office, rank, or natural excellence.
From the honor God's majesty requires, the same respect differs in its whole kind.

lemmas.gloss: to differ in the whole kind

choices.why: The excellence in view is grace and glory, not mere reputation.
